model.name: Digital Signature / Proof
model.purpose: Describe a digital signature or cryptographic proof as reusable context that can be mixed into any host entity: the proof instance and its binding to an exactly identified payload, the signer or creator attribution it carries, the signature method and profile used, and the evidence produced when the proof is verified, preserved, projected or reviewed for disposition.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-034 models the facts an agent needs to understand, record, inspect and operate a digital signature or proof without owning any cryptographic, PKI, identity, records or legal machinery. In scope are: the proof instance and its exact payload binding; the asserted signer or creator and the verification method or certificate reference used to attribute it; the signature method, algorithm suite, canonicalization and declared profile; references to supporting evidence objects (certificates, status responses, time-stamp tokens, evidence records); verification runs with pinned inputs and separated per-dimension verdicts; comparison between runs; additive preservation and renewal evidence; projection of proofs and evidence into selected bindings with declared losses; and reported readiness for disposition. The model is storage-format and interface neutral: ASN.1, XML, JSON, CBOR, Markdown, Git, MCP and document databases are projections of the same semantics. All statements are recorded as observations attributable to a party at a time, never as self-asserting warrants.
in_scope: The proof instance: its binding to an exactly identified payload or payload version, its detached, enveloped or enveloping placement, and its serialization form
Signer or creator attribution carried by the proof, including the asserted verification method or certificate reference, declared proof purpose or commitment type, and any domain or challenge scoping
The signature method: algorithm and cryptosuite identifiers, key parameters, transform and canonicalization chain, and the declared signature or proof profile
References to supporting evidence objects associated with the proof: certificates, revocation status responses, time-stamp tokens and evidence records, held as references with binding parameters
Verification runs: pinned inputs, separated cryptographic, trust, evidence-completeness, policy, identity and legal-conclusion dimensions with machine-readable reasons, and comparison between runs
Preservation and renewal evidence added over the life of the proof, recorded additively without altering the original proof
Projection of a proof and its evidence into a selected binding, with an explicit register of projection losses and refusal of unsupported critical semantics
Reported readiness of a proof and its evidence for disposition, expressed as conditions rather than as an instruction to delete
out_of_scope: Cryptographic execution: key generation, hashing, signing, signature primitive computation, key storage, key revocation and hardware or remote signing device operation
Certification authority, trust service provider and time-stamping authority operation, including certificate issuance, revocation decisions, trust-list governance and supervision status conferral
Identity proofing, credential issuance, authentication events and the binding of a natural or legal person to a key beyond recording the attribution asserted by the proof
Host record and business-document lifecycle, approval workflow, versioning policy and content semantics of the signed payload
Legal determination of enforceability, admissibility, non-repudiation as a legal effect, or conferral of a regulated status such as qualified electronic signature
Audit-trail construction, audit-record retention and the evidentiary chain of the audit system itself
Execution of deletion, erasure, media sanitisation and retention-schedule authorship or approval
Runtime policy evaluation engines, authorization decision points and enforcement of access or trust decisions

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent holds the general cryptographic integrity and evidence abstraction shared across proof kinds. WM-XCT-034 specialises only the signature or proof subject and inherits, rather than restates, the parent's generic evidence vocabulary.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Certificate, trust anchor and revocation status model (PKI)
boundary_notes.distinction: This model carries references to certificates, trust anchors and status responses, plus the run-specific parameters that pinned them. Certification path construction policy, trust anchor governance, revocation decision-making and certificate lifecycle stay in the PKI model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Time-stamping and trust service provider model
boundary_notes.distinction: Time-stamp tokens and preservation service outputs are referenced as evidence objects with their policy identifiers and accuracy claims. Operating a time-stamping authority, asserting time accuracy and supervising a preservation service belong to the trust service model.

This model records which policy identifier and version was pinned for a run and which parameter values applied. Authoring, approving, publishing and enforcing validation or signature policies belong to the policy model.

This model reports readiness conditions such as outstanding preservation obligations and blocking references. Retention schedules, disposition authority, freeze and hold administration and deletion execution belong to the records model.

Verification runs and evidence registrations are recorded here as domain facts with their own identity. Constructing, sealing, protecting and retaining an audit trail over those facts is owned by the audit model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Host document, credential or transaction model
boundary_notes.distinction: WM-XCT-034 is mixed into a host entity and describes the proof over it. The host's identity, states, versions and business meaning remain with the host model; only the payload binding reference is held here.

sources.title: ETSI EN 319 102-1 V1.4.1 Electronic Signatures and Trust Infrastructures (ESI); Procedures for Creation and Validation of AdES Digital Signatures; Part 1: Creation and Validation
sources.relevance: Normative source for the validation model: validation constraints, validation time, proof of existence, best-signature-time, the basic/with-time/with-long-term-data/with-archival-data validation processes and the status indication and sub-indication vocabulary. Retrieved via ETSI's public deliver path; direct automated download was refused by the server, so the version and identifier were confirmed against independent indexes and against implementations that cite it clause by clause.

sources.title: ETSI TS 119 102-2 V1.3.1 Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures (ESI); Procedures for Creation and Validation of AdES Digital Signatures; Part 2: Signature Validation Report
sources.relevance: Defines the reportable structure of a validation result: per-signature validation report, validation status with main and sub indication, signature identifier, signer information, constraints evaluation report, validation time information and the validation objects (certificates, CRLs, OCSP responses, time-stamps, evidence records) used. Anchors the run-record and report-projection findings.

sources.title: RFC 3161 Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP)
sources.relevance: TSTInfo fields (policy, messageImprint, serialNumber, genTime, accuracy, ordering, nonce, tsa) and the verifier's obligations. Grounds proof-of-existence evidence units, their provenance parameters and the rule that time-stamp verification is a distinct dimension from payload integrity.

sources.title: RFC 4998 Evidence Record Syntax (ERS)
sources.relevance: Archive time-stamp chains and sequences, reduced hash trees, and the two renewal modes (time-stamp renewal and hash-tree renewal). Grounds additive preservation evidence, evidence coverage sets and the requirement to renew before an algorithm weakens.

sources.title: RFC 6283 Extensible Markup Language Evidence Record Syntax (XMLERS)
sources.relevance: XML binding of evidence records with explicit canonicalization method and supporting cryptographic information lists. Demonstrates that the same preservation semantics have multiple bindings and that canonicalization choice is a verification-affecting parameter, not a formatting detail.

sources.title: RFC 5280 Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Certificate and Certificate Revocation List (CRL) Profile
sources.relevance: Section 6 certification path validation inputs, including trust anchor information, current date and time, initial policy set and name constraints. Establishes that trust-path evaluation is parameterised and time-dependent, which is why trust anchors and as-of time must be pinned per run.

sources.title: RFC 6960 X.509 Internet Public Key Infrastructure Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP)
sources.relevance: SingleResponse fields thisUpdate, nextUpdate and producedAt, and the client acceptance rules for freshness and responder authorisation. Grounds the status-evidence freshness parameter and the separation of evidence production time from observation time.

sources.title: RFC 7515 JSON Web Signature (JWS)
sources.relevance: Protected versus unprotected headers, multiple signatures, detached payload (Appendix F) and the crit header rule that an unrecognised critical extension makes the signature invalid. Grounds projection loss, payload separation on export and refusal of unsupported critical semantics.

sources.title: Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0 (W3C Recommendation)
sources.relevance: Proof attributes (cryptosuite, created, expires, verificationMethod, proofPurpose, domain, challenge, previousProof), the verify-proof algorithm and its verification result structure with warnings and errors, proof sets and proof chains, and transformation or canonicalization as a precondition of verification. Provides a non-PKIX verdict vocabulary for comparison.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-102 Recommendation for Digital Signature Timeliness
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Establishes that signature validity depends on key status at signing time rather than verification time, and that an independent trusted timestamp is required to make that determination. Grounds the separation of claimed signing time, best-signature-time and validation time.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-131A Revision 2 Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Acceptable, deprecated, disallowed and legacy-use categories and the asymmetry between signature generation and verification policy (for example SHA-1 disallowed for generation but permitted for legacy verification). Grounds algorithm-policy pinning and renewal-horizon calculation.

sources.title: Digital Signature Service (DSS) documentation
sources.relevance: Reference implementation documentation for the four report projections (diagnostic data, detailed report, simple report, ETSI validation report), validation policy constraint groups, indication and sub-indication reporting, and the distinction between validation time, best-signature-time and proof of existence. Demonstrates that the same run yields several non-equivalent report projections.

sources.title: DSS Cookbook: Signature validation (esig/dss source documentation)
sources.organization: European Commission, Digital Building Blocks (esig/dss project)
sources.relevance: Enumerates validation levels (basic signatures, timestamps, long-term data, archival data), constraint groups, revocation freshness handling, cryptographic suite sunset dates with fail versus warn behaviour, and best-signature-time derivation. Used to identify operational parameters that must be pinned for a run to be reproducible.

sources.title: ETSI TS 119 511 Electronic Signatures and Trust Infrastructures (ESI); Policy and security requirements for trust service providers providing long-term preservation of digital signatures or general data using digital signature techniques
sources.relevance: Preservation profiles, preservation goals (preservation of digital signatures, preservation of general data, augmentation) and preservation evidence policy governing how preservation evidence is created and validated. Treated as an alignment target for evidence-unit provenance; direct automated download was refused, so no clause-level conformance is claimed.

sources.title: ETSI TS 119 512 Electronic Signatures and Infrastructures (ESI); Protocols for trust service providers providing long-term data preservation services
sources.relevance: Protocol surface of a preservation service, including preservation object identifiers, evidence retrieval and deletion operations. Used to justify holding a stable external preservation identifier and to keep preservation execution and deletion outside this model. Direct automated download was refused, so no clause-level conformance is claimed.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Lifecycle requirement categories (capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata, reporting) with must-have and should-have designations, distinguishing program requirements from system requirements. Grounds the disposition-readiness finding and the separation between reporting readiness and executing disposal.

bundles.name: Verification Runs, Verdicts and Comparison
bundles.description: Everything needed to request, record, interpret and compare a verification of a digital signature or proof: the pinned inputs that make a run reproducible, the time basis and proofs of existence the verdict is anchored to, the separated verdict dimensions with machine-readable reasons, the run record and its report projections, and the disciplined comparison of two runs over the same subject.
bundles.rationale: Authoritative validation procedures treat a verification result as the output of a parameterised process, not as an intrinsic property of the signature: the outcome depends on validation time, trust anchors, algorithm constraints, revocation freshness and available proofs of existence, and is reported as an indication with a sub-indication rather than a boolean (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-006, SRC-012). A model that stores only a pass or fail flag is therefore unfalsifiable and non-reproducible, which is why the run inputs, the time basis and the per-dimension reasons are modelled as first-class context.

layers.name: Run Inputs and Time Basis
layers.description: The determinacy surface of a verification: the parameters that must be fixed before evaluation, and the time values and proof-of-existence assertions the evaluation is anchored to.

findings.name: Verification run request and determinacy pins
findings.description: The complete set of caller-supplied and defaulted inputs that make a verification run reproducible: the validation or as-of time, the exact payload and payload version the proof is asserted to cover, the trust anchor set and the snapshot of it that was consulted, the cryptographic suite policy including algorithm sunset dates, the maximum permitted age of status evidence, and the pinned identity of the evaluating tool and its data sources. Path validation inputs are parameterised and time-dependent (SRC-006) and constraint groups differ per policy (SRC-012, SRC-013), so an unpinned run cannot be re-derived or contested.

questions.text: Which inputs must be pinned before a verification run is accepted as reproducible?
answer_data: Required pin list with per-pin presence status
Rejection reason when a required pin is absent
Policy identifier that defines the required pin list

questions.text: Which exact payload version is the proof asserted to cover, and how is that version identified?
answer_data: Payload reference to the host record and its version identifier
Digest algorithm and digest value used as fixity for that version
Placement of the proof relative to the payload (detached, enveloped, enveloping)

questions.text: Which trust anchor set was consulted, and which snapshot of it applied at run time?
answer_data: Trust anchor set reference and snapshot identifier or publication instant
Source of the snapshot as declared by its publisher
Whether the snapshot was retrieved live or replayed from a stored copy

questions.text: Under whose cryptographic suite policy, and with which sunset dates, was this run evaluated?
answer_data: Policy identifier and version
Per-algorithm status (acceptable, deprecated, disallowed, legacy verification only) and sunset date
Party accountable for the policy content

questions.text: What maximum age of certificate status evidence was permitted relative to the as-of time?
answer_data: Freshness limit expressed as a duration, or an explicit statement that freshness was not constrained
Actual age of each status object used
Whether nextUpdate was present and honoured

data_elements.name: Validation (as-of) time
data_elements.description: The instant the verification is evaluated against; determines certificate validity assessment and status evidence acceptance.

data_elements.name: Payload binding reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the host payload and the exact version or revision the proof covers, held as a reference into the host model.

data_elements.name: Payload fixity value
data_elements.description: Digest algorithm identifier and digest value used to confirm that the payload presented at verification is the version the proof covers. Fixity, not identity.

data_elements.name: Trust anchor set pin
data_elements.description: Reference to the trust anchor set or trust list plus the snapshot identifier or publication instant actually used.

data_elements.name: Cryptographic suite policy pin
data_elements.description: Reference and version of the algorithm policy, including the per-algorithm sunset dates applied in this run.

data_elements.name: Status evidence freshness limit
data_elements.description: Maximum accepted age of revocation or status evidence relative to the as-of time; absence means unconstrained and must be recorded explicitly.

data_elements.name: Evaluating tool pin
data_elements.description: Name, version and configuration digest of the software that produced the result, plus versions of any external data sources it consulted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A run request is a parameter set, not a document: every element is either a scalar, a duration, or a reference into a model that owns the referenced object (trust anchor sets, policies, host payloads, tool inventories). Materialising it as an artifact would create a second, competing copy of trust-list and policy content that this model has no authority to maintain. The pins are therefore held inline on the run record and resolved by reference at read time.

findings.name: Time basis and proofs of existence
findings.description: Separation of the distinct time values a verdict can be anchored to: the claimed signing time asserted by the signer, the best-signature-time derivable from trusted evidence, the validation or as-of time, and the instants at which each evidence object was produced versus observed. Signature validity turns on key status at signing time rather than verification time, and that determination requires independent time evidence (SRC-010); proofs of existence are carried by time-stamp tokens and evidence records (SRC-003, SRC-004) and are what allow a signature to remain assessable after certificate expiry or revocation (SRC-001, SRC-013).

questions.text: Which time value is this verdict anchored to, and why was that value selected?
answer_data: Selected anchor kind (claimed signing time, best-signature-time, validation time)
Selection rule and the policy that mandated it
Alternative anchors that were available but not used

questions.text: Which referenced objects establish that the proof existed before a given instant?
answer_data: List of proof-of-existence assertions with the covered object, the instant and the evidence reference
Evidence kind (time-stamp token, archive time-stamp, evidence record, external attestation)
Whether each proof-of-existence evidence object itself verified in this run

questions.text: How is an unproven claimed signing time kept distinguishable from a proven one?
answer_data: Assertion strength flag per time value (self-asserted, third-party attested, chained to a preserved evidence sequence)
Evidence reference supporting any non-self-asserted value
Statement recorded when no independent time evidence exists

questions.text: When was each status or evidence object produced, and when was it observed and recorded here?
answer_data: Production instant reported by the producing service
Observation or ingestion instant recorded by this model
Retrieval channel and whether the object was replayed from cache

data_elements.name: Claimed signing time
data_elements.description: Time asserted within the proof by the signer or creator; carries no independent weight on its own.

data_elements.name: Best signature time
data_elements.description: Earliest instant at which it can be trusted that the proof existed, derived from available proof-of-existence evidence.

data_elements.name: Proof-of-existence assertion
data_elements.description: Structured assertion naming the covered object, the instant proven, the supporting evidence reference and the evidence kind.

data_elements.name: Evidence production time
data_elements.description: Instant the referenced evidence object was generated by its producing service, as reported by that service.

data_elements.name: Evidence observation time
data_elements.description: Instant this model retrieved or registered the evidence object, recorded separately from its production time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Time values and proof-of-existence assertions are derived scalars and references over evidence objects that are owned elsewhere: the time-stamp token or evidence record is the artifact, and it belongs to the preservation-evidence finding or to the referenced trust service. Producing a separate time artifact here would duplicate that evidence and invite the two copies to diverge, so the time basis is stored inline on the run record and resolved against the referenced evidence units.

layers.name: Verdicts, Run Records and Comparison
layers.description: How a verification result is expressed, stored and later compared: separated verdict dimensions with machine-readable reasons, an immutable run record with report projections, and a change-attributing comparison between runs.

findings.name: Separated verdict dimensions and machine-readable reasons
findings.description: A verification result is recorded as independent dimensions rather than a single verdict: cryptographic integrity of the proof over the bound payload; trust path to an accepted anchor; completeness of supporting evidence; conformance to the pinned policy including algorithm constraints; identity or attribution of the asserted signer; and legal conclusion. Each dimension carries its own status and reason codes drawn from a declared code system. Authoritative validation procedures already distinguish failure from indeterminacy and require a sub-indication explaining which condition was not met (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-012), and non-PKIX suites report verification alongside separate warning and error lists (SRC-009). The legal dimension is always recorded as not determined by this model unless an external authority record is referenced.

questions.text: Which verdict dimensions are reported separately, and what exactly does each one assert?
answer_data: Dimension name with a one-sentence scope statement per dimension
Status per dimension (passed, failed, indeterminate, not evaluated)
Explicit not-evaluated marking where a dimension was out of the run's remit

questions.text: Which machine-readable reason code and code system explains each non-passing dimension?
answer_data: Reason code value and the identifier and version of its code system
Human-readable gloss carried alongside, never instead of, the code
Mapping note where a code was translated from a different code system

questions.text: How may dimension results be combined, and what must never be inferred from a single dimension?
answer_data: Declared aggregation rule and the party that set it
Explicit non-inference statements (for example cryptographic pass does not imply trust or attribution)
Whether an aggregate summary was produced and by which rule version

questions.text: Who owns the legal conclusion about this proof, and what does this model record in its place?
answer_data: Reference to the external authority, determination record or jurisdictional regime, when one exists
Fixed not-determined-here status when no such record exists
Factual inputs recorded for that external decision without a conclusion attached

data_elements.name: Verdict dimension result
data_elements.description: One dimension of the verdict: dimension name, status, ordered reason codes, and references to the evidence objects that drove the status.

data_elements.name: Dimension status
data_elements.description: Coded status per dimension distinguishing passed, failed, indeterminate and not evaluated; indeterminate is never collapsed into failed.

data_elements.name: Reason code
data_elements.description: Machine-readable reason attached to a non-passing dimension, resolvable within a declared code system.

data_elements.name: Reason code system reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the vocabulary a reason code belongs to, so codes remain resolvable across bindings.

data_elements.name: External legal determination reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a determination made by an authority outside this model; never a conclusion authored here.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dimension results are structured fields of a run record and are meaningless detached from the pinned inputs that produced them; the transportable document is the run record's report projection, declared in the run-record finding. Emitting dimension results as a standalone artifact would let a verdict circulate without its inputs, which is precisely the failure mode the separation of dimensions exists to prevent.

findings.name: Verification run record and report projection
findings.description: The stored record of one verification: run identity, the digest of the pinned inputs, the dimension results, references to every evidence object consulted, the asserting party, and the start and end instants of evaluation. The record is an observation attributable to a party at a time, not a warrant of validity, and it is projected into report bindings for exchange. Standardised report structures carry the validation status, signer information, constraint evaluation, time information and the validation objects used (SRC-002); reference implementations show that a single run legitimately yields several non-equivalent report projections at different levels of detail (SRC-012, SRC-013).

questions.text: How is a single verification run identified so it can be cited later without ambiguity?
answer_data: Run identifier and the system that issued it
Digest over the canonical pinned input set
Subject reference identifying the proof and payload version verified

questions.text: Under what conditions, if any, may a stored run record be changed after it is written?
answer_data: Append-only rule with the permitted correction mechanism
Superseding record reference and correction reason when a record is withdrawn
States a run record can occupy (provisional, complete, withdrawn) and who may set them

questions.text: What must a report projection of a run contain to remain self-describing away from its store?
answer_data: Mandatory sections: subject reference, pinned inputs, dimension results with reason codes, asserting party, times
Projection binding identifier and its version
Back-reference to the run identifier and the input digest

questions.text: Which party asserted this run, and under what declared competence or accreditation?
answer_data: Asserting party identifier and role
Declared competence, accreditation or service-level basis, or an explicit none
Whether the asserting party also operated the signing or timestamping service (conflict flag)

questions.text: How long must a run record stay retrievable to support later comparison and review?
answer_data: Minimum availability period and the rule reference that sets it
Owner of the retention rule outside this model
Consequence recorded when a prior run is no longer retrievable

data_elements.name: Verification run identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for one run, issued by the authoritative verification system or assigned by the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Pinned input digest
data_elements.description: Digest over the canonical serialisation of the pinned run inputs, enabling detection of any later input drift.

data_elements.name: Asserting party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party that ran and stands behind the verification, with its declared role.

data_elements.name: Run execution instants
data_elements.description: Start and completion instants of the evaluation, recorded separately from the as-of validation time.

data_elements.name: Consulted validation object reference
data_elements.description: Reference to each certificate, status response, time-stamp token or evidence record consulted during the run.

data_elements.name: Run record state
data_elements.description: State of the record itself: provisional, complete or withdrawn-and-superseded; never a state of the signature.

artifacts.name: Signature validation report
artifacts.description: A self-describing projection of one run record for exchange or human review, carrying the subject reference, pinned inputs, per-dimension results with reason codes, consulted validation objects, asserting party and times. Multiple projections of differing detail may exist for the same run and are never treated as independent verdicts.
media_or_form: structured validation report following a standardised report schema
detailed technical report enumerating each evaluation step
concise summary report for human review
verification result object in a proof-suite native form
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the run identifier issued by the authoritative verification system, plus a projection binding identifier and projection sequence number. Where no master-system identifier exists, the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID. Filenames, report titles and dates are never used as identity.

findings.name: Comparison of verification runs and change attribution
findings.description: The disciplined comparison of two runs over the same proof and payload version, producing a per-dimension difference set in which each difference is attributed to a cause class: elapsed time and newly available proofs of existence, trust anchor set change, status evidence change, policy change, algorithm sunset, evidence added by preservation, or evaluating tool change. The earlier verdict is never overwritten or invalidated; it remains a true statement about the inputs that produced it. Cause classes follow directly from the parameters that authoritative procedures make variable (SRC-001, SRC-006, SRC-011, SRC-013).

questions.text: Are these two runs comparable at all, and against which invariants was that decided?
answer_data: Invariant check results for subject proof identity, payload version and fixity value
Comparability verdict with a refusal reason when invariants differ
Note recording any deliberate cross-version comparison and its limits

questions.text: Which cause class explains each dimension difference between the two runs?
answer_data: Per-dimension difference with an assigned cause class
Evidence reference supporting the assignment (changed pin, added evidence unit, new status object)
Unattributed differences flagged rather than forced into a class

questions.text: Why does a later run never overwrite or retract the earlier recorded verdict?
answer_data: Statement that each run is scoped to its own pinned inputs
Ordering relation between runs without an implied precedence of truth
Rule identifying which run a consumer should rely on for a given question and as-of time

questions.text: How much of the observed change is attributable to non-cryptographic causes?
answer_data: Count of differences per cause class
Flag when the cryptographic dimension is unchanged while other dimensions moved
Comparison window between the two run execution instants

data_elements.name: Compared run reference
data_elements.description: Reference to each of the two run records being compared, in a declared earlier and later order.

data_elements.name: Comparability invariant check
data_elements.description: Result of checking that both runs address the same proof, the same payload version and the same fixity value.

data_elements.name: Dimension difference
data_elements.description: One dimension whose status or reason set differs between the two runs, with both prior and later values retained.

data_elements.name: Change cause class
data_elements.description: Coded attribution of a difference to elapsed time, trust anchor change, status evidence change, policy change, algorithm sunset, added preservation evidence, tool change or unattributed.

artifacts.name: Verification run comparison record
artifacts.description: A record of one comparison between two run records: the invariant checks that established comparability, the per-dimension differences with prior and later values, the assigned cause classes, and any differences left unattributed. It adds interpretation and never restates either run's verdict as superseded.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the comparison identifier issued by the system of record, ordered by comparison sequence and always carrying the two compared run identifiers. Where no master-system identifier exists, the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID.

bundles.name: Preservation Evidence, Projection and Disposition Readiness
bundles.description: Everything needed to keep a proof assessable over time and to move or retire it responsibly: additive preservation and renewal evidence, the calculated assessment of evidence coverage and renewal need, export projection into a selected binding with declared losses and separated access, and the reported readiness of a proof for disposition.
bundles.rationale: Cryptographic algorithms weaken over archival periods, so long-term assessability depends on adding time-stamp and evidence records before compromise rather than on the original proof alone, and renewal is defined as an additive operation over the existing evidence sequence (SRC-004, SRC-005). Preservation services are external providers with their own profiles, goals and object identifiers (SRC-014, SRC-015), and disposal is a distinct lifecycle category with its own program and system requirements (SRC-016). Bindings differ in the semantics they can carry, and an unrecognised critical extension invalidates a signature rather than degrading it (SRC-008), which makes projection loss a first-class fact.

layers.name: Additive Preservation Evidence and Renewal
layers.description: Evidence units added over the life of a proof to keep it assessable, and the derived assessment of whether current evidence still covers it.

findings.name: Preservation evidence unit and renewal record
findings.description: One unit of evidence added to keep a proof assessable: an archive time-stamp token, an evidence record with its archive time-stamp chains and sequence, collected validation material, or evidence returned by an external preservation service. Units are recorded append-only and never modify the original proof bytes. Two renewal kinds are distinguished because they cover different risks: re-stamping the previous time-stamp addresses signature-algorithm weakening, while re-hashing the data objects together with the prior evidence addresses digest-algorithm weakening and starts a new chain (SRC-004, SRC-005).

questions.text: What guarantees that registering this evidence unit leaves the original proof byte-identical?
answer_data: Pre-registration and post-registration fixity values of the original proof
Storage rule prohibiting in-place modification of the original proof
Rejection reason recorded when a submitted unit would require rewriting the proof

questions.text: Which renewal kind does this unit represent, and what does it re-cover?
answer_data: Renewal kind (initial evidence, time-stamp renewal, hash-tree renewal, external preservation augmentation)
Set of objects re-covered by the unit
Digest and signature algorithms the unit introduces

questions.text: How does this unit chain to the evidence already recorded for the same proof?
answer_data: Predecessor unit reference and chain or sequence position
Whether the unit continues an existing chain or opens a new one
Detected break in continuity, if any, with the affected interval

questions.text: Which external service produced this evidence unit, and under which declared policy?
answer_data: Producing service reference and its policy or profile identifier
Preservation object identifier or token serial issued by that service
Production instant reported by the service and observation instant recorded here

questions.text: Which digest algorithm and canonicalization does this unit depend on for later verification?
answer_data: Digest algorithm identifiers used across the unit
Canonicalization or transform method identifier where the binding requires one
Known status of each algorithm under the pinned algorithm policy

data_elements.name: Evidence unit identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the evidence unit, preferring the identifier issued by the producing preservation or timestamping service.

data_elements.name: Evidence unit kind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of unit: time-stamp token, archive time-stamp, evidence record, collected validation material, or service-issued preservation evidence.

data_elements.name: Renewal kind
data_elements.description: Whether the unit is initial evidence, a time-stamp renewal, a hash-tree renewal or an external augmentation.

data_elements.name: Evidence coverage set
data_elements.description: References to every object the unit demonstrably covers, including the proof, the payload version and prior evidence units.

data_elements.name: Chain and sequence position
data_elements.description: Position of the unit within its archive time-stamp chain and of that chain within the sequence.

data_elements.name: Producing service reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external timestamping or preservation service and the policy or profile under which the unit was issued.

artifacts.name: Preservation evidence unit
artifacts.description: The stored evidence object itself, retained byte-exact as received from its producing service, together with the registration metadata that places it in the chain and sequence for a given proof. Registration records the object; it does not generate, re-sign or re-time it.

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the identifier issued by the producing service (for example the preservation object identifier or the token serial number scoped to that authority). Where no such identifier exists, the adopting Dimension assigns a UUID or ULID and records the producing service reference alongside. Sequence position is ordering metadata, never identity, and the production date is never used as an identifier.

findings.name: Evidence coverage and renewal-need assessment
findings.description: A calculated, always re-derivable assessment of whether existing evidence still covers a proof: the interval currently covered, discontinuities in the chain, the sunset horizon of every digest and signature algorithm appearing in the chain under the pinned policy, and the latest date by which a further evidence unit must be obtained for coverage to remain unbroken. Renewal must occur before the relevant algorithm weakens (SRC-004), algorithm status changes over time and differs between generation and verification (SRC-011), and implementations distinguish hard failure from advisory warning around sunset dates (SRC-013). The assessment recommends; obtaining evidence is an external service action.

questions.text: Through which interval is this proof currently covered by recorded evidence?
answer_data: Coverage start and end instants derived from the evidence sequence
Assessment as-of time and the algorithm policy version used
Explicit uncovered statement when no evidence unit exists

questions.text: Which condition would trigger a renewal recommendation, and at what horizon?
answer_data: Trigger condition (algorithm sunset, coverage expiry, policy change, chain break)
Recommended-by date and the lead time applied
Severity distinguishing advisory from blocking

questions.text: Where are the discontinuities or weak links in the recorded evidence chain?
answer_data: Interval and predecessor or successor references for each detected gap
Units relying on an algorithm now disallowed for verification
Confidence note where a gap cannot be distinguished from missing records

questions.text: Which party is accountable for acting on a renewal recommendation?
answer_data: Accountable party reference and its role
External preservation service that would supply the evidence
Escalation path recorded when the recommendation lapses unaddressed

data_elements.name: Evidence coverage interval
data_elements.description: Derived start and end instants of continuous evidence coverage for the proof.

data_elements.name: Algorithm sunset horizon
data_elements.description: Per-algorithm date after which the pinned policy no longer accepts the algorithm, together with the algorithm's current status.

data_elements.name: Renewal-by date
data_elements.description: Latest date by which a further evidence unit must be obtained for coverage to remain unbroken.

data_elements.name: Evidence chain gap
data_elements.description: One detected discontinuity, with its interval and the units on either side.

data_elements.name: Assessment basis
data_elements.description: As-of time, algorithm policy version and evidence set revision the assessment was computed from.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This assessment is entirely derived from the registered evidence units and the pinned algorithm policy, and it goes stale the moment either changes or the clock advances. Persisting it as an artifact would create a document that looks like preservation evidence but carries none, inviting consumers to rely on a stale renewal-by date. It is therefore held as inline computed context that must be recomputed with a stated as-of time and policy version on every read.

layers.name: Export Projection and Disposition Readiness
layers.description: Moving a proof and its evidence into another binding without silent semantic loss, and reporting whether the proof and its evidence are ready to be retired.

findings.name: Export projection, access separation and loss register
findings.description: Projection of a proof and selected evidence into a target binding, where authorisation to disclose the payload and authorisation to disclose signer identity are evaluated separately, every semantic the target binding cannot carry is enumerated in a loss register, and any unsupported critical semantic causes refusal rather than silent downgrade. The refusal rule follows the established treatment of unrecognised critical extensions as invalidating rather than ignorable (SRC-008); payload separation follows detached-payload practice (SRC-008) and the report-object model that carries validation objects independently of the signed document (SRC-002). An exported proof asserts nothing about its own verification: any verification statement must travel as a separately identified run record.

Requesting party and the stated purpose of the export

findings.name: Disposition readiness report
findings.description: A reported readiness state for retiring a proof and its evidence, combining the host record's lifecycle state, the applicable retention rule reference, any active legal hold or disposition freeze, outstanding preservation obligations from an external preservation arrangement, and blocking inbound references such as evidence units or run records that depend on the proof. Disposal is a distinct lifecycle category with its own program and system requirements and its own freeze semantics (SRC-016); preservation arrangements impose their own obligation periods and their own deletion surface (SRC-014, SRC-015). This model reports conditions and never executes, authorises or schedules deletion.

composition.purpose: WM-XCT-034 is registered under WM-XCT-006 and specialises only the signature or proof subject. The generic integrity and evidence abstraction, and any vocabulary shared across proof kinds, stay in the parent; this entry does not restate them.

composition.target: Certificate, trust anchor and revocation status model
composition.purpose: Carry references to certificates, trust anchor sets and status responses together with the run-specific parameters that pinned them (snapshot selector, freshness limit). Path construction policy, trust anchor governance, revocation decisions and certificate lifecycle remain owned by the target.

composition.target: Time-stamping and preservation trust service model
composition.purpose: Carry references to time-stamping and preservation services, their policy or profile identifiers and the object identifiers they issue. Service operation, accuracy assertions, supervision status and preservation execution remain owned by the target.

Carry the pinned policy identifier, version and the parameter values that applied to a run. Authoring, approving, publishing and enforcing validation or signature policies, and operating any runtime evaluator, remain owned by the target.

composition.target: Cryptographic algorithm and suite policy registry
composition.purpose: Reference algorithm status and sunset dates used in run pinning and renewal assessment. Maintaining the registry, setting transition dates and distinguishing generation from verification policy remain owned by the target.

Reference retention rules, disposition freezes and holds as inputs to readiness reporting. Schedule authorship, disposition authority, hold administration and execution of disposal remain owned by the target.

Link run records, evidence registrations and export events to entries in an external audit trail. Construction, sealing, protection and retention of the audit trail remain owned by the target; this model records domain facts only.

Obtain separately resolved payload-disclosure and identity-disclosure authorisations for export projections. Authorisation decision-making, policy evaluation and enforcement remain owned by the target.

composition.target: Host document, credential or transaction model
composition.purpose: Attach proof, verification and preservation context to any host entity through the payload binding reference, without redefining the host's identity, versions, states or business meaning.
Alignment target for report projections of a run record. Field-level correspondence is declared per projection and conformance is claimed only where a documented test exists.

composition.target: Evidence record syntaxes in ASN.1 and XML bindings
composition.purpose: Alignment target for preservation evidence units and chain or sequence semantics, including the distinction between time-stamp renewal and hash-tree renewal.

composition.target: Data integrity proof model for linked-data credentials
composition.purpose: Alignment target for non-PKIX proof attributes and verification result vocabulary, including proof purpose, verification method, proof sets and proof chains, so the verdict dimensions remain expressible outside a certificate-based setting.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names an accountable owner for verification run records and for the preservation evidence register, and that owner is organisationally distinct from any party operating the signing, timestamping or preservation services whose output is recorded.

Before the first run record is issued, the Dimension declares the authoritative master system for each identified object class here (run records, evidence units, exports, readiness reports) and the fallback identifier scheme where no master system exists.

The Dimension publishes and versions the code systems used for verdict dimension statuses, reason codes, change cause classes, projection loss classes and blocking condition classes, and commits to preserving unknown codes on round-trip.
The Dimension declares which trust anchor sources and algorithm policy sources it will pin, and how snapshots of them are retained so that a past run can be re-derived.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers are namespaced by the adopting Dimension and are opaque: no date, no algorithm name, no verdict value and no host record name may be encoded in an identifier. External identifiers (preservation object identifiers, token serial numbers scoped to an issuing authority, certificate serial plus issuer) are kept in their issuer's namespace and never rewritten; where a local surrogate is needed it records the external identifier alongside it.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-034 in the world-model record plane, navigation path NAV.XCT.SIG, domain tag XCT.SIG
Parent registry entry WM-XCT-006, which owns the generic integrity and evidence abstraction this entry specialises
Dimension-published code system registry for verdict, reason, cause, loss and blocking-condition vocabularies

canonicalization_rules: The original proof and every registered evidence unit are stored byte-exact as received; no canonicalization, re-encoding, whitespace normalisation or re-serialisation is applied to them, because the digest that verification depends on is taken over the received bytes.

Canonicalization applies only to model-authored records (pinned input sets, run records, comparisons, readiness reports): fields sorted by identifier, absent optional fields omitted rather than nulled, codes carried as code plus code-system-version pairs.
Where a binding requires a transform or canonicalization method for verification, the method identifier is recorded as a pinned parameter of the run, not chosen at read time.
Time values are stored as received with their original offset preserved; a normalised UTC form may be derived for ordering and comparison but never replaces the recorded value.
patch_rules: Run records, comparison records, evidence units and export events are append-only. A correction is a new record that references and supersedes the earlier one with a stated correction reason; the earlier record remains readable.
No patch may alter a stored verdict, a pinned input set or the bytes of an original proof or evidence unit; a patch that would require this is refused with a machine-readable code.
Derived context (renewal assessments, readiness states) is not patched but recomputed, always carrying a fresh as-of time and the policy and evidence-set revisions used.
Adding a later evidence unit or a later run never rewrites earlier records; the relationship between them is expressed through chain position and comparison records.
compatibility_rules: Adding a verdict dimension, reason code, cause class or loss class is a minor change; removing one, or redefining what an existing code asserts, is a breaking change requiring a new code system version.
Codes and fields that a consumer does not recognise are preserved verbatim on read and re-emit; silent dropping of unknown codes is a conformance failure.
Report and export bindings are versioned independently of the records they project; a projection always carries its binding identifier and version plus the source record identifier.
A conformance claim against any external standard is made only where a documented test result exists; otherwise the relationship is recorded as an alignment with the known divergences listed.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the object: the preservation or timestamping service's own object identifier or token serial scoped to its issuing authority, the verification system's run identifier, or the exporting system's export identifier.
Governed global identifier or IRI where the object is published under a governed namespace, such as a resolvable identifier for a validation report or an issuer-scoped verification method IRI.
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension where neither of the above exists, recorded together with the producing service reference so the surrogate remains traceable.
Content digests are recorded as fixity values and may support equality checks, but a digest is never promoted to an identifier; a date, an as-of time or a sequence number is never an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are recorded in RFC 3339 format with at least whole seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; a value lacking an offset is rejected rather than assumed to be local or UTC. Event time and observation time are recorded separately whenever they can differ: the event time is the instant the external fact occurred or was produced (time-stamp genTime, status response producedAt or thisUpdate, claimed signing time, host disposal instant), while the observation or ingestion time is the instant this model retrieved, evaluated or registered it. Run execution instants and the as-of validation time are distinct fields and are never conflated; where only one time is known, the other is recorded as absent rather than copied.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts (validation reports, comparison records, evidence units, export packages, loss registers, readiness reports) are named by the identifier of the object they belong to plus a monotonic sequence number scoped to that object, plus the binding identifier and version where a projection exists. Sequence numbers convey order only and never identity or precedence of truth; dates, verdict values and status words must not appear in the name.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artifact carries a fixity value with its digest algorithm identifier, computed on receipt and re-checked before any read that feeds a verification, comparison, export or readiness computation. A fixity mismatch on an original proof or evidence unit halts the operation and is recorded as a blocking condition; it is never repaired by re-serialisation. Fixity values are refreshed only by adding a new value with a stronger algorithm alongside the existing one, never by replacing the recorded history.

policies: A verification verdict is always scoped to its pinned inputs and its as-of time; a verdict recorded without those pins, or read without them, is treated as uninterpretable rather than as a pass or fail.

Indeterminate is never collapsed into failed or into passed, and no single dimension may be reported as the overall validity of a proof; consumers requesting a boolean receive a refusal with the dimension set instead.
Preservation evidence is additive only: no operation in this model may modify, re-sign, re-time or re-encode an original proof or a previously registered evidence unit.

Legal conclusions, qualified-status determinations and admissibility judgements are never authored here; the model records the factual inputs and, where one exists, a reference to an external determination.
Presence of a proof, an evidence unit or an export never implies verification; any verification statement must be a referenced, identified run record with its pins intact.

Physical deletion, hold release, audit-trail construction, cryptographic execution and trust enforcement are performed by referenced external systems; this model reports conditions and records outcomes reported back to it.

read: Reading a run record returns its pinned input set and dimension results together; partial reads that omit the pins are refused.
Derived context (renewal assessment, disposition readiness) is recomputed on read with a stated as-of time, policy version and evidence-set revision, never served from a cached value without those.
Reading an original proof or evidence unit re-checks its fixity value first and surfaces any mismatch to the caller.
Payload content and signer identity are read through separately authorised paths; a read of proof metadata never implies a read of the payload.
create: A run record may be created only from a complete pinned input set with a computed input digest and a named asserting party.
An evidence unit may be registered only with its producing service reference, policy or profile identifier, coverage set and pre- and post-registration fixity confirmation for the original proof.
A comparison record may be created only after its comparability invariants have been checked and recorded, including failed checks.
An export event may be created only after payload-disclosure and identity-disclosure authorisations have been resolved independently and the loss register has been produced.
update: Stored verdicts, pinned input sets and received bytes are immutable; a correction is a new superseding record carrying a correction reason and a reference to the record it supersedes.
Record state may advance from provisional to complete, or to withdrawn-and-superseded, and each transition records the actor and the observation time.
Reference fields may be repointed only when the target model reports a governed identifier change, and the prior identifier is retained in the record.
Recomputing a derived assessment is not an update: it produces a new dated assessment and leaves any earlier one intact.
delete: This model does not execute deletion. It stores a retention intent for each record class and reports readiness; execution belongs to the adopting Dimension's storage and records-management systems, and the retention schedule, disposition authority and hold administration belong to the referenced records retention and disposition model.

Default retention intent: an original proof and its evidence units are retained at least as long as the host record's retention rule and at least as long as any preservation arrangement obligation, whichever is longer; run records, comparison records, export events and readiness reports are retained at least as long as the proof they describe so that past verdicts remain re-derivable.

When disposal is executed externally, a tombstone is retained containing the proof identifier, the subject and payload version references, the disposition reason, the effective instant, the executing system reference and the identifiers of dependent records; payload content, signer identity detail and proof bytes are not retained in the tombstone.

A record subject to an active legal hold or disposition freeze, or referenced by an undischarged preservation obligation or a dependent evidence chain, is reported as blocked; this model neither overrides nor releases such a condition, and hold release is owned by the issuing authority in the records model.
Retention of any audit trail covering these operations is owned by the referenced audit model and is not set, shortened or extended here.

responsibilities: Resolves payload-disclosure and identity-disclosure authorisations separately for each export request
Confirms the projection loss register is complete and that unsupported critical semantics resulted in refusal rather than downgrade
Ensures every export carries the non-implication statement and, where a verdict is included, a resolvable run record reference

roles.name: Disposition reviewer
responsibilities: Reviews dated readiness reports and confirms which blocking conditions are genuine and which are stale references
Routes confirmed readiness to the external executing system and records the outcome reported back
Confirms that tombstone content is sufficient to keep dependent evidence chains and run records consistent after disposal

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted per scope and per facet: metadata about a proof (identifiers, method, chain position, verdict dimension statuses) is separable from signer identity detail and from payload content, and a grant over one facet never implies a grant over another. Read access to a run record always includes its pinned inputs, since a verdict without pins is misleading.
exceptions: A disposition reviewer may read blocking-condition metadata across proofs without payload or signer identity access, because readiness review needs breadth, not content.

An export requester may receive a detached export with the payload withheld when payload disclosure is denied but proof and evidence disclosure is permitted; the loss register records the withheld payload as an explicit projection loss.
Under an active legal hold, read access may be widened to a named hold-handling party by the authority owning the hold; this model records the widening as a fact and does not grant it.
Where signer identity disclosure is denied, verdict dimension statuses may still be released with identity-dimension reason codes reduced to a non-identifying form, and the reduction is recorded.
audit_requirements: Every read of payload content, every read of signer identity detail, every export event and every registration or correction is emitted as a domain fact with actor, purpose, scope and observation time, for recording by the referenced audit model.
Refusals matter as much as successes: refused exports, refused registrations, fixity mismatches and refused boolean-verdict requests are emitted with their machine-readable codes.
This model states what must be emitted and does not construct, seal, protect or retain the audit trail; audit-record integrity and retention are owned by the audit model.

required_fields: Code system registry URL for verdict, reason, cause and loss vocabularies
Non-implication notice stating that presence of a proof or export implies nothing about its verification
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type and Owner before any operation is attempted
Read the Specification URL to obtain the model boundary, in-scope and out-of-scope statements, and the composition links that name externally owned concerns
Read the Storage type URL to learn how records, original proofs and evidence units are physically held and how byte-exactness and fixity are guaranteed
Read the Interface URL for the read, create, update and reporting surface, including which operations refuse rather than default
Read the Processes URL for the run, comparison, registration, export and readiness procedures and their preconditions
Read the code system registry before interpreting any status, reason, cause or loss code, and preserve unrecognised codes verbatim

coverage.claim: This structure covers the operating surface of a digital signature or proof as evidenced by the cited standards and first-party implementation documentation: parameterised verification with separated verdict dimensions and machine-readable reasons, an explicit time basis distinguishing claimed, proven and evaluation times, immutable run records with non-authoritative report projections, comparison of runs with change attribution, additive preservation and renewal evidence, derived renewal assessment, lossy-by-declaration export projection with separated payload and identity disclosure, and reported disposition readiness. It deliberately holds cryptographic execution, PKI and trust service operation, policy authorship and enforcement, identity proofing, audit-trail construction, legal determination and deletion execution outside the boundary as referenced concerns. It is not a claim of conformance to any cited standard and not a claim of completeness for signature creation practice, hardware attestation or post-quantum proof composition.

checklist.notes: Run, evidence unit, export and readiness records each have their own identifier with a stated priority: producing-service or master-system identifier first, then governed IRI, then Dimension-assigned UUID or ULID. Digests are explicitly demoted to fixity and dates are explicitly excluded from identity.

Record-level lifecycle only: provisional, complete, withdrawn-and-superseded, with append-only correction. The lifecycle of the host record, of certificates and of preservation services is referenced, not modelled; readiness reporting reads host lifecycle state rather than driving it.

Payload binding, evidence chain and sequence position, run-to-comparison links, export-to-loss-register dependency and blocking inbound references are all modelled. Twelve composition links name the externally owned neighbours explicitly.

Claimed signing time, best-signature-time, validation as-of time, evidence production time, observation time and run execution instants are distinct fields. RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset is mandated and offset-less values are rejected.

Every evidence unit carries its producing service and policy identifier; every run carries its asserting party, tool pin and consulted object list; every trust anchor and policy pin carries a snapshot identifier so a past run can be re-derived.

Asserting party for runs, accountable party for renewal, producing service for evidence, hold-issuing authority and external execution owners for disposal are all named. Five service roles are separated, with the evidence custodian deliberately distinct from the signing or timestamping operator.

Verification is modelled as a parameterised process with six separated dimensions, machine-readable reason codes bound to a versioned code system, comparability invariants for run comparison, and an explicit prohibition on collapsing indeterminate into pass or fail.

Deny by default with facet separation between proof metadata, signer identity detail and payload content; export evaluates payload and identity authorisations independently; four exceptions are enumerated, including identity-reduced verdict release.

Retention intent, tombstone content, blocking conditions and readiness reporting are modelled here; schedule authorship, hold administration and physical deletion are assigned to the records model and the Dimension's storage systems, and audit retention to the audit model.

Report and export bindings are versioned and self-describing; projection losses are enumerated by class; unsupported critical semantics force refusal; unknown codes must survive round-trip. Alignments to a standardised report structure, to evidence record syntaxes and to a linked-data proof model are declared without conformance claims.

Evidence units are additive and byte-preserving, with the two renewal kinds distinguished by the risk each addresses, coverage sets recorded per unit, and chain discontinuities surfaced rather than smoothed over.

Key generation, signing, hashing, primitive computation and revocation are performed by external evaluators and PKI components. The model records their reported outcomes and pins, and owns no execution or enforcement.

Enforceability, admissibility and qualified-status conferral are reported as not determined here unless an external determination is referenced. Only the factual inputs to such a decision are recorded.

No primary source is cited here for recording hybrid or composite signatures, dual-algorithm proof chains or migration evidence across a post-quantum transition. The algorithm-horizon fields would carry the dates but the composition semantics of a hybrid proof are unmodelled and must not be presented as canonical.

Handwritten, biometric, notarial and hardware-attestation proof forms are within the plain reading of the registry purpose but no cited source grounds their verification or preservation semantics; the verdict dimensions may not transfer to them unchanged.

known_omissions: Hybrid and composite post-quantum proofs: no structure for dual-algorithm proof composition, migration evidence or the interaction between a hybrid proof and an evidence chain built under a single-algorithm assumption.

Distributed-ledger or transparency-log anchoring as an alternative proof-of-existence source; the proof-of-existence assertion structure would accept it, but no cited source grounds the trust and freshness parameters such an anchor would need.

Signature creation-side context (device attestation, remote or server-side signing assurance, sole-control evidence) is referenced only as attribution asserted by the proof and is not modelled as an operating surface.
Countersignature, multi-party and threshold verification orchestration: proof sets and chains are aligned to, but ordering obligations across parties and quorum semantics are not modelled.
Content-level media provenance bindings, where a proof covers derived renditions rather than a fixed payload version, are excluded; the payload binding assumes an exactly identified version.
Quantitative assurance or confidence scoring of a verdict; only categorical statuses and reason codes are modelled, deliberately, since no cited source defines a comparable scale.
conflicts: Verdict shape conflicts across communities: certificate-based validation procedures report an indication with a sub-indication and treat indeterminate as a first-class outcome, while the linked-data proof model returns a boolean verified flag with warning and error lists. This model keeps dimensions separate and refuses boolean requests, which will not round-trip cleanly into a boolean-only consumer.

Algorithm status conflicts between regimes: transition guidance permits legacy verification with an algorithm that is disallowed for generation, while a signature validation policy may treat the same algorithm as failing after its sunset date. The pinned policy decides, and the run record must show which regime was applied.

Revocation freshness expectations conflict with real signature profiles: a zero freshness interval is specified in some referenced material while implementations default to ignoring freshness to accommodate baseline signatures without timestamps. The freshness limit is therefore a required explicit pin, including an explicit unconstrained value.

Preservation obligations and records disposal schedules can conflict: a preservation arrangement may require retention beyond the host record's schedule. This model reports both as blocking conditions and does not resolve the conflict, which remains an authority question for the records model.

Detached-payload exports satisfy disclosure minimisation but reduce later verifiability; refusing an export to preserve verifiability can conflict with a lawful disclosure limit. The loss register records the tension rather than resolving it.
regional_assumptions: The indication and sub-indication vocabulary, validation constraint groups and preservation profile concepts derive from the European trust services framework; the semantics are reusable but the specific code values and any qualified-status notion are region-bound and must not be assumed elsewhere.

Algorithm transition categories (acceptable, deprecated, disallowed, legacy use) reflect United States federal guidance; other jurisdictions publish different horizons for the same algorithms, so an algorithm horizon is only meaningful with its policy reference attached.

Disposition, freeze and transfer requirement structure reflects United States federal records management practice; national archives and sector regulators elsewhere define different disposal categories and hold mechanics.

Legal hold semantics are assumed to originate outside the model in every jurisdiction, but which party may issue and release a hold varies; the readiness report therefore records the issuing authority rather than assuming one.

Time zone and offset handling assumes the recording system can obtain the original offset; where a source system stores only local wall-clock time, values are rejected rather than coerced, which may reduce coverage in some legacy estates.
adversarial_checks: Does any bundle, layer, finding or function claim ownership of a referenced target's semantics? Checked against every composition rationale: verification consumes an external evaluator's reported outcomes rather than executing cryptography; policy is pinned by reference rather than authored or enforced; holds and retention schedules are mirrored read-only; audit emission requirements are stated but the audit trail is not constructed or retained; deletion is reported as readiness and executed elsewhere. The evidence-registration function was the closest call and is constrained to recording an externally produced unit with byte-level additivity checks.

Could a consumer derive a bare pass or fail from this structure and circulate it without its inputs? Blocked at three points: dimension results are inline on the run record rather than a standalone artifact, report projections must carry the pinned inputs and the run identifier to be self-describing, and a boolean request is refused with the dimension set. The residual risk is a downstream system that flattens the projection anyway, which the model can detect only through the input digest.

Does adding preservation evidence or running a later verification ever mutate history? No operation updates a stored verdict, a pinned input set or received bytes; corrections are superseding records; comparison records add interpretation and explicitly do not retract the earlier verdict; renewal assessments are recomputed rather than patched. Fixity is re-checked before every read that feeds an operation.

Is any date, digest or verdict value used as an identifier? Identity priority names the master-system identifier first and explicitly demotes digests to fixity and excludes dates; serial naming forbids dates, verdict values and status words; sequence numbers are declared to convey order only. No local identifier in this model contains a date-like component.

Does export leak by default? Payload and identity disclosure are separately authorised, deny-by-default applies per facet, unsupported critical semantics cause refusal rather than silent downgrade, and every export carries a fixed statement that presence implies nothing about verification. The known weakness is that a recipient may still present the export as validated, which is why any verdict must travel as a referenced run record.

Is the structure falsifiable? Two dimensions are recorded as genuine gaps (post-quantum hybrid composition, non-cryptographic and hardware-attested proof forms), two ETSI preservation specifications could not be machine-retrieved and are therefore treated as alignment targets rather than clause-level support, and five standing conflicts between source regimes are recorded rather than reconciled.
